## Headline read — the most replicable thing

Bill operated via a disciplined three-touch outbound sequencing on cold prospects: case study email + intro-to-product email + social proof/urgency email, always closed with a direct phone number and call-to-action. He then moved fast to calls, took detailed discovery notes on properties and competitive context, and kept leads warm through follow-up questions and solicitor-escalation problem-solving—never over-explaining, always moving toward the next commitment.

## Conversation openers

### cold outbound (list-based, Droughtmaster association)

**Pattern.** Open with a highly relevant peer success story (same breed/region), quantified upside, close with casual phone number and 'feel free to call' permission structure.

**Verbatim:**
> "Bill from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out, as I found your email on the Droughtmaster website and thought you might be interested to hear that Queensland producers Karen and Rob Scanlan, used their Droughtmaster herd to generate soil carbon credits. Their story here: https://agriprove.io/fysh-cp-cs. Using grazing management and pasture improvements they saw a massive 400% lift in carry capacity and earned 3,559 credits valued at over $124,000 at current ACRU price. Talk about the perfect management of a versatile breed that delivered straight to their bottom-line. If you want to chat further feel free to call me on +61 483 946 496…"

### cold outbound (second touch in sequence, warm)

**Pattern.** Pivot from story to product positioning as second email in sequence. Reframe as 'better introduce AgriProve' to show self-awareness that first email was story, now comes context.

**Verbatim:**
> "Following up yesterday's email it occurred to me that better introduce AgriProve! We are Australia's leading soil carbon developer, providing breeders with the technology, tools, and insights to increase productivity, enhance soil health, and generate a new revenue stream doing it."

### cold outbound (third touch, final)

**Pattern.** Third email uses self-aware gate-keeper message ('Final time I'll personally reach out (promise)') paired with second related case study and product feature tie-in (e.g., Ceres Tags + Ready Graze tool + deferred payment).

**Verbatim:**
> "Final time I'll personally reach out (promise). I couldn't miss the opportunity to let you know about this: Queensland producers Kylie and Lance Stephenson have been credited an average of 3.9ACCUs/Ha/Yr using their Droughtmaster herd as the tool!"

### referral / warm inbound (post-DAF event / mention)

**Pattern.** Open with gratitude for time, reference to specific context (e.g., 'Attended DAF carbon day, AgriProve was mentioned'), attach developer checklist and point to Help Centre + YouTube for self-serve verification.

**Verbatim:**
> "It was great to speak with you yesterday afternoon. Thank you very much for taking the time out of your day to chat with me. As discussed, I wanted to follow up with some additional information for you to take a look at."

## Discovery questions

- **Property-specific deep-dive: total area, usable land, land use (grazing/farming mix), existing land management practices, competitor context, readiness signal (core count, timeline).** — _surfaces:_ Bill captures granular asset detail (total vs. usable acreage, soil type, existing competitive positioning) and competitive intelligence in first call—not in follow-up. Allows him to tailor next steps and identify if lead is truly qualified (e.g., 'keen to do something' + 'very high quality hot lead' = priority).
  > "[NOTE on Geoff Nicol] Cattle grazing property in Injune 5000Ha total, 4000ha usable, 1000 virgin range scrub country. No farming, grazing only. Mix of breeding and background. High quality fertile grazing. Attended DAF carbon day, AgriProve was mentioned there. Have had conversations with two other providers (CL and someone). CL said 2000Ha suitable, otherwise too steep or too treed. Keen to do something. 250 cores (8ha per core). Brigilow regrowth - thin. Very high quality hot lead."
- **Legal/friction point escalation: When lead raises solicitor review concern, offer names of solicitors with prior contract experience rather than deflecting or saying 'we'll help later'.** — _surfaces:_ Rather than create friction, Bill solves the objection by providing named references and reducing uncertainty. This keeps the deal warm and signals he understands the legal-review process is real.
  > "[Dale Mulholland] Would you have all the legal documents that I could have my solicitor look over, or is that something that we do later. → Bill responds: I have chased up a few farmers who have projects with us to find out what solicitors they have used. You could try the following, all of which have experience review these kinds of contracts: Rees R & Sydney Jones / CLO Lawyers Toowoomba / Thynne + Macartney Lawyers Brisbane"
- **Platform account creation as mini-discovery tool: Ask prospect to create free AgriProve Platform account before call, with an explicit gate-lower ('shouldn't take more than 2 minutes, you can skip adding in stock numbers').** — _surfaces:_ Bill uses product as a discovery lever, not a close. Prospect's willingness to create account signals intent. Bill can then frame the call as joint exploration of their own data, not a pitch.
  > "To assist in the assessment of your soil carbon opportunity and increase the value of our conversation tomorrow, can you please create a free AgriProve Platform Account here: https://eoi.agriprove.io/eoi/emission/nextSteps. It shouldn't take more than 2 minutes and you can skip adding in stock numbers etc. to move through it quickly. Once set up I will be able to take a look at the property opportunity with you."

## Transitions

### From cold outbound sequence (3 emails) to call → discovery call with property + competitive detail capture

After 3rd email, Bill schedules outbound call at a specific time slot, provides meeting invite with Teams link, and sends a pre-call email with a micro-action (platform account creation) to warm up the prospect 24hrs before.

> "[To Michael Coughlan] Thank you for your time this afternoon and I look forward to giving you a call tomorrow. I have sent out a meeting invite for a call at 11:30am NSW time. To assist in the assessment of your soil carbon opportunity and increase the value of our conversation tomorrow, can you please create a free AgriProve Platform Account here…"

### From discovery call with hot lead → immediate send of collateral + comparison checklist

Same-day or next-day email post-call. Attach 'developer checklist' to help them compare providers, point to Help Centre and YouTube, signal that Bill is not the only resource (reduces perceived pressure).

> "As you are considering several providers, I have attached our developer checklist. This details some good questions to ask and can help understand the points of difference. Secondly, I would suggest heading to our Help Centre: https://help.agriprove.io/ to have a look through some of our answers to our most common queries."

### From prospect raises legal/solicitor friction → proactive resource solve (solicitor names) + gentle check-in

Rather than escalate or defer, Bill provides named reference list and then follows up 2–3 weeks later with a low-pressure check-in ('How have you gone getting in touch with solicitors?').

> "[2025-05-21] How have you gone getting in touch with solicitors? → [2025-05-26] I hope the rain hasn't cause to many troubles on your property. How are you going?"

### From deal stalling / prospect in solicitor review stage → warm handoff to Head of Growth with explicit transition language

When Bill transitions out of AgriProve (to CERES TAG), he explicitly introduces Harry Chapman as Head of Growth, acknowledges shared work ('AgriProve and CERES TAG work closely together'), and positions handoff as partnership, not abandonment.

> "I will be transitioning out of my AgriProve at the end of this week. Fortunately, I will be keeping in close contact with the team, as AgriProve and CERES TAG work closely together. To make sure you are in safe hands, I would like to take the opportunity to introduce you to Harry Chapman, Head of Growth, copied into this email."

- **Immediate platform account creation micro-commitment pre-call (lowers friction for full discovery, allows Bill to frame conversation around prospect's own data, not a pitch).** _[high]_
  Evidence: Michael Coughlan thread. Bill sends pre-call email with 'create free account in 2 minutes' gate, holds the call at exact time, then delivers property summary doc + soil carbon report within days. Prospect moves from initial call to multi-property scoping without resistance.
- **Developer comparison checklist + self-serve resources (Help Centre, YouTube) as confidence-builder, not objection-handler. Signals AgriProve is not afraid of due diligence.** _[high]_
  Evidence: Geoff Nicol (hot lead). Bill sends checklist same-day post-call: 'As you are considering several providers, I have attached our developer checklist.' Geoff remains engaged (no drop-off to competitor) despite CL already having quoted.
- **Solicitor friction solve with named peer references (Rees R Jones, CLO Lawyers, Thynne + Macartney) rather than 'we'll provide docs later.' Removes the single biggest legal sticking point for agricultural deals.** _[high]_
  Evidence: Dale Mulholland. Raises solicitor concern in first email; Bill responds within days with three named firms + URLs. Deal stays warm for 7+ months despite slow solicitor review. Follow-up note (June 26) confirms 'Solicitors are still looking over it. We should expect an email from him with queries coming soon'—deal not dead.
- **Warm handoff to Head of Growth with explicit co-ownership language ('I will be keeping in close contact with the team, as AgriProve and CERES TAG work closely together'). Prevents deal loss during rep transition.** _[high]_
  Evidence: Dale Mulholland, Geoff Nicol. Bill transitions to CERES TAG (May 26) but explicitly introduces Harry Chapman and signals continuity. Ben Payne takes over a few weeks later with note confirming deal is still live ('Solicitors are still looking over it').
- **Repetition of land-size-specific messaging (Southern Queensland 'carbon capital' positioning for >400ha properties). Regional soil-type specificity (Vertosols, Dermosols) + track record (57 projects, 10,265 hectares, 22,689 ACCUs = $800K) is used as re-engagement bait, not initial pitch.** _[moderate]_
  Evidence: Graham & Sharron Rawlinson (December re-engagement by Ben, building on Bill's May outreach). Ben leads with Southern Queensland soil science, then track record. This is conversion-driver validation: regional proof is stronger than generic product.

## Customer archetypes — who they engaged well

### Droughtmaster breeder / grazer (warm list, association-based inbound)

**Characteristics.** Mixed grazing + background cattle operation, 3000–5000ha, likely in QLD/NSW, heard of AgriProve via DAF event or industry association, competitive context (other carbon developers), moderate to high readiness signal (willing to discuss).

**Approach.** 3-touch sequence: peer case study (Scanlan, same breed, quantified upside) → product intro → second case study (Stephenson) + financing innovation (Ceres Tags + deferred payment). Phone number and 'feel free to call' closes each email.

**Example.** Graham & Sharron Rawlinson, Todd Alexander Cormack

### Commercial grazing operation with mixed properties / regions (multi-property, higher complexity)

**Characteristics.** 3+ properties across different rainfall/soil zones, existing agronomic data (FieldMargin maps), family operation (e.g., Michael, Anna, Isabelle), slower decision timeline (expects scoping report + solicitor review), higher due diligence burden.

**Approach.** Pre-call platform account creation → discovery call with detailed property notes → multi-property scoping document (PDF) delivered same week → soil carbon report with cross-property analysis. Follow-up on report understanding, offer call to review. Handoff to Head of Growth.

**Example.** Michael Coughlan (Tarabah Livestock Co)

### High-potential hot lead (DAF event, organic interest, competitive context known)

**Characteristics.** Attended DAF carbon day, competing offers already in hand (e.g., CL), clear readiness (e.g., 'keen to do something,' already discussed core count), property is ideal soil + high usable area, property detail known (5000ha total, 4000 usable, specific soil type).

**Approach.** Same-day call, immediate post-call collateral (developer checklist), developer positioning (help them compare, not just pitch AgriProve). Do not over-explain; give them the tools to vet all providers. Keep warm via low-pressure check-ins.

**Example.** Geoff Nicol (Ninderra Grazing Co, 'Very high quality hot lead')

### Referral / warm introduction (peer-introduced, e.g., 'Dave Waterson's mate')

**Characteristics.** Trust is pre-built, but prospect still needs education on legal/contract process, likely first time exploring carbon projects, may have solicitor questions early.

**Approach.** Warm opening (acknowledge referrer, thank for time), immediately address friction points (solicitor checklist, named law firms), schedule discovery call at prospect's convenience. Offer flexibility ('available both tomorrow and Thursday').

**Example.** Dale Mulholland ('Dave Waterson's mate')
